ledger.claim: The driver's explanation for stopping roughly 200 metres short of the pin - that 'the last stretch is a bus lane' - is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and there is no artifact behind it. The traffic_advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00536-01, is MISSING from the bundle, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the rider discloses that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Nothing on file names a road, expressway segment or junction that the optimal route traverses for this window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion of bad traffic carries no weight and is discarded. The driver's excuse therefore explains nothing, exonerates nothing and reduces no excess.

Nor can the driver fall back on a rider-requested detour or stop. The chat_log for this trip, EV-CHAT-00536, is COMPLETE and records zero messages - first_message_at and last_message_at are both null and message_count is 0 - so there is no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the route under POL-RD-04, and the driver's 'I told them where to go' exists only as an unsworn statement with no recorded message behind it. Both exculpatory routes open to the driver, POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-04, are closed on this record.

The substance of the rider's complaint is confirmed by the platform's own record, not merely by her account: the trip_record's dropoff is labelled 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier', so the recorded completion point is not the destination the rider pinned, and the driver's own statement concedes the same 200 metre gap. That dropoff-point discrepancy is what POL-RD-05 governs, but the record carries no dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so the clause's re-quoted optimal cannot be run on this bundle; and POL-RD-01, which measures only the excess between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, registers nothing about a trip that ended short of its destination. The rider's grievance - a trip not completed to the point she booked - is therefore documented and unpriced by the arithmetic.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to invent a distance excess, because the trace is unimpaired and states the opposite. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 3.09 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 3.2 km, an excess of -0.11 km, or -3.44%, so neither establishment test in POL-RD-01 (greater than 20% of optimal, and greater than 0.8 km absolute) is satisfied and POL-RD-02's recomputation has no deviation to run on. The rider's case on this record is not a POL-RD-02 refund and she does not press one; she asks the tribunal to decide the short-ended trip that is actually recorded.

ledger.claim: The platform's own derivation records NO deviation on this trip: the measured excess is -0.11 km against a 0.8 km absolute threshold and -3.4375% against a 20% proportional threshold. Under POL-RD-01 a route deviation is ESTABLISHED only when the excess exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceeds 0.8 km; here the driven distance is actually shorter than the booking optimal, so both gates fail by a wide margin. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The governing figure is 3.09 km (derived.deviation.trace_distance_km), set against a booking optimal of 3.2 km. Even on the trip_record's own convenience copy the driven distance is 3.1 km, again below the 3.2 km optimal. There is no positive excess to measure on any reading of the record, so POL-RD-01 cannot be satisfied.

The trace that produced that measurement is unimpaired for policy purposes: 73 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) limbs is met (no gap over 90 s, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 s), so the trace is a sound and admissible basis for the POL-RD-01 threshold test and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The rider's own narrative and the dropoff field both describe a SHORTFALL, not an excess: the recorded dropoff is 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier', matching the rider's account that the driver stopped about 200 m before the pin. POL-RD-01 measures deviation as actual_distance_km minus optimal_distance_km, so a stop short of the pin is by construction incapable of establishing a deviation — it can only reduce the measure, which is exactly what the -0.11 km figure shows.

No pickup or dropoff relocation is on the record: trip_record.dropoff_amended_at and pickup_amended_at are both null, so no amended endpoint and no amended optimal exist under POL-RD-05. The booked 3.2 km optimal stands as the correct comparator, there is no re-quote to re-run the threshold against, and no substitute figure needs to be derived.

The in-app chat export for this trip contains zero messages (message_count 0, empty messages array). There is therefore no recorded rider instruction and no waypoint_hint on which POL-RD-04 could operate, and no rider message by which the dropoff point could have been relocated. Neither the rider-requested-detour clause nor any chat-based route excuse is available on this record to either side, and nothing in the chat undermines the driver.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires on this bundle. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00536); the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); the trip timestamps are consistent (pickup 13:05/13:10, start 13:11:40, end 13:23:40); and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The case is therefore fully rulable and must not be diverted to a human reviewer.

The traffic advisory for this trip is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the driver does not invoke POL-RD-03 or rest on any external traffic cause, so nothing turns on its absence. Under POL-RD-13 an assertion that cites no advisory identifier is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5).

The fare ledger reconciles line by line: base fare 3.80 + distance 2.33 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80 = 10.29 charged, with no ERP gantry charged, no toll and no airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom line and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no billing-integrity refund is available under POL-RD-09(4), and no pass-through correction is due under POL-RD-09.

The driver's profile discloses no repeat deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, a ratio of 0.000 against the 0.05 limb and 0 against the count-of-3 limb. The POL-RD-06 test is not satisfied, so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral is licensed.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. She has not discharged it: the only trace on file records -0.11 km, and her rider_profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0, which neither adds a corroboration requirement nor supplies any support for the claim. The burden never shifts to the driver.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION. NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: on this rider-filed dispute, where fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, it leaves the 10.29 charge standing exactly as it is and returns nothing to the rider. The present payment state — the fare in the driver's hands — is preserved.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the central fact: the trip ended about 200 metres short of the pin, and the platform's own dropoff label records it ('Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier'). The question is what the route-deviation policy does with that, and the answer is nothing that pays out.

Under POL-RD-01 a deviation exists only where the distance driven exceeds the booking-optimal distance by more than 20% AND by more than 0.8 km. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (POL-RD-01 makes trace_distance_km govern over the trip record's rounded convenience copy): 3.09 km driven against a 3.2 km optimal, an excess of -0.11 km (-3.44%). Both gates fail — the trip was shorter than optimal, not longer — so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 never runs. For transparency only: had it run it would have compared a charged_total of 10.29 against a recomputed fare of 9.24, a refund of 1.05; that figure is not payable because there is no deviation to trigger it.

The fare is correct line by line: base 3.80 + distance 2.33 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80 = 10.29 charged, with no ERP gantry, toll or airport surcharge to correct, so POL-RD-09 gives nothing back either and no billing-integrity referral arises.

The driver's explanation — that the last stretch is a bus lane — is an external-traffic assertion. There is no traffic advisory on file for this trip (EV-ADVIS-00536-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and reduces no excess, and POL-RD-03 cannot be run to exonerate anything. The chat log is empty, so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 is available either, and no amended endpoint exists for POL-RD-05.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (73 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no inter-fix gap over 90 seconds), and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers fires — in particular the absent advisory was cited by no party as an exculpatory ground, so POL-RD-13(1) applies and this is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The case is therefore decided on the record, and there is no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern finding (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips).

Result: NO_ACTION. The SGD 10.29 charged stands exactly as it is; nothing is refunded and nothing is paid to the driver. The rider's grievance — being set down short of her pin and having to run the last stretch with two small children — is real and is recorded on the trip record itself, but the route-deviation policy prices excess distance, not a short stop, and on this record there is no excess to price. If the rider wishes to pursue the short dropoff as a service-quality concern, that is a separate matter from this fare.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
